header.userPrompt:
Enforce one principle across the web module's forms: every user-entered input on a `FormData` is a `FormField` over a validated primitive, never a raw value. Document the principle in the frontend reviewer, then fix the five `FormData` classes that still hold raw inputs. Web module only. Do NOT change any API request/response models, and do NOT add anything to `lib/common` or `lib/api`. Keep every new validated type under `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits`.

## The principle (document it, then apply it)

On a `FormData` subclass, every field that holds a value the user can enter or choose must be a `FormField[T]` whose `T` is a validated primitive, and every such field must appear in the `fields` list so `isValid` covers it. The ONLY members allowed to be a raw (non-`FormField`) value are:
- a `Boolean` (a checkbox/toggle needs no validation), and
- a genuine pass-through context id the form carries but the user never edits (e.g. `rowId`, `receiptId`) — these are constructor inputs, not form fields, and must not be bound to any editable control.

Everything else is a `FormField` over a bounded/validated primitive:
- a text value uses a `WrappedString`-style primitive with a maximum length,
- a number uses a bounded primitive (positive, capped digits/decimals, like `PositiveBigDecimal`),
- a date/time uses a parsed primitive (like `ExpLocalDate`),
- an id the user picks uses a field whose validator enforces the id's format (blank or a well-formed id), and a pick-or-create selection uses `ExistingOrNewValue` resolved through a shared resolver.

Flag a raw `String`, `BigDecimal`, `Int`, `UUID`, `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, or tuple/list of those held directly on a `FormData` as an input (anything other than a `Boolean` or a non-edited context id).

Add this as a new section to `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` (it belongs with the existing FormData rules: "A FormData model carries a spec", "Required fields are modeled on the field", "Seed validated fields with the raw value"). Write it in the same "flag X / Not: Y" style as the other sections, and extend the frontmatter `description` line with a short clause for it. Reviewer files hold review instructions only, no roadmap or future notes.

## Reference files (study first, copy their shape exactly)

- Primitive templates: `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpWrappedBigDecimal.scala`, `.../PositiveBigDecimal.scala`, `.../ExpLocalDate.scala`, `.../ExpRuleFields.scala` (for `ExpRulePattern`), `.../ExistingOrNewValue.scala`.
- Library `WrappedString` primitive to mirror for text: `lib/common/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/common/models/CategoryDescription.scala` (bounded text, `MaxLength`, optional parse). Do NOT edit lib; clone the shape into web.
- Inputs: `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/inputs/expInputs.scala` and `.../inputs/inputs.scala`.
- Autocomplete component (js interop internal, Props plain Scala, required vs optional via `SelectionShape`): `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/core/widgets/ExpValidatedAutocompleteInput.scala`.
- Resolvers (use these, never inline find-or-create): `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/CategoryResolver.scala`, `.../MerchantResolver.scala`.
- The FormData + component shape to match, and its spec: `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BankRowRuleFormData.scala`, `.../SavingsGoalFormData.scala`, `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/BankRowRuleForm.scala`, `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BankRowRuleFormDataSpec.scala`.
- The reviewer rules you must satisfy: `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`.

## New primitives + inputs to build (web only)

1. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpNotes.scala` — a bounded free-text primitive, built like `CategoryDescription` (a `WrappedString`-style clone living in web; mirror the shape of the existing web primitives). `MaxLength = 500` to match `CategoryDescription`. Provide `validate` / `parse` / `trusted`, a `given TextValidator`, and a `given` optional validator (blank = `None`), the same way `PositiveBigDecimal` / `ExpLocalDate` expose theirs. Notes are optional everywhere they are used.
2. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpLocalTime.scala` — a parsed time-of-day primitive mirroring `ExpLocalDate`, wrapping `java.time.LocalTime` and parsing ISO `HH:mm` (accept `HH:mm:ss` too) via `LocalTime.parse`; invalid input yields a clear error. Provide the same `validate`/`parse`/`trusted`/`given TextValidator`/`given` optional validator. Time is optional everywhere.
3. A picked-id selection field for a pick-EXISTING-only control (no create): a `FormField[Option[UUID]]` whose validator treats blank as `None` and otherwise requires a well-formed `UUID` (format check). Add a small reusable validator/primitive under `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms` (e.g. `ExpOptionalId` with a `given TextValidator[Option[UUID]]`) plus a matching input object. This is for the expenses-page merchant dropdown, which is a `mui.Select` of existing merchants, NOT a create path, so `ExistingOrNewValue` does not apply there.
4. Add the corresponding input objects to `expInputs.scala` (`NotesInput`/`OptionalNotesInput`, `TimeInput`/`OptionalTimeInput`, the id-selection input) following the existing ones. No hardcoded React key inside any reusable input; derive it from the field name.

Each new primitive gets a spec under `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms` (plain ScalaTest, no jsdom): valid parses and round-trips, over-limit/malformed rejected, optional validator maps blank to `None`. Name describe blocks by the method only (e.g. `"validate"`, `"parse"`), never type-qualified like `"ExpNotes.validate"` — the repo convention and the `tests` reviewer require method-only descriptions.

## The five FormData classes to fix

For each, convert every raw input member into a `FormField` over the right primitive, add it to `fields`, seed it from source data with the raw value (no `.trim`/`.take` to squeeze a value in, no `.trusted` on user input), and update the page that renders it to use the validated inputs and gate submit on `isValid`. Resolve any pick-or-create through the shared resolvers. Keep all js/MUI interop inside components. Each changed FormData gets its `*FormDataSpec` updated/added (submitRequest valid vs None, and any transition).

1. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/ExpenseFormData.scala` + `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala`:
   - `merchantId: String` -> `FormField[Option[UUID]]` using the id-selection field (ExpensesPage uses a `mui.Select` of existing merchants with a "(none)" option; keep it a select, just make it a validated optional-id field).
   - `time: String` -> `FormField[Option[ExpLocalTime]]`.
   - `notes: String` -> `FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]`.
   - `splits: List[(String, String)]` -> a list of a small split-row case class of `FormField`s: category as the id-selection `FormField[Option[UUID]]` (the split category comes from a `mui.Select`) and amount as `FormField[PositiveBigDecimal]`. Flatten these row fields into `fields` so `isValid` covers them. Keep add/remove-row behavior. The cross-field "splits must cover the amount" rule legitimately stays at the page level (a form-level rule no single field can express); keep it where it is.
2. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/ReceiptConfirmFormData.scala` + `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/receipts/ReceiptsPage.scala`:
   - Collapse `merchantId: String` + `merchantInput: String` + `parsedMerchantName: Option[String]` into one merchant pick-or-create field `FormField[Option[ExistingOrNewValue[MerchantName, UUID]]]` (ReceiptsPage uses a free-solo Autocomplete, so it is a genuine select/create), resolved through `MerchantResolver` at submit. If the parsed merchant name is still needed as a creation seed, carry it via the field's input value, not a separate raw member.
   - `time` -> `FormField[Option[ExpLocalTime]]`; `notes` -> `FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]`.
   - `splits: List[(String, String, String)]` (categoryId, categoryInput, amount) -> list of split-row `FormField`s: category as `FormField[Option[UUID]]` (or `ExistingOrNewValue` if that split category control is a create path; it is a select, so the optional-id field) and amount as `FormField[PositiveBigDecimal]`. Flatten into `fields`.
   - `rowId: Option[UUID]` stays a pass-through context member (not a field).
3. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BulkExpenseFormData.scala` + `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala`:
   - `notes: String` -> `FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]`. (merchant/category already migrated.)
4. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BankRowRefundFormData.scala` + `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateRefundForm.scala`:
   - `notes: String` -> `FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]`.
5. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BankRowExpenseFormData.scala` + `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala`:
   - `notes: String` -> `FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]`.
   - `rulePattern: String` -> `FormField[ExpRulePattern]` (the primitive exists in `ExpRuleFields`). The rule opt-in is a `Boolean` and may stay a raw Boolean. Model the pattern as a validated field; it is only read at submit when the opt-in Boolean is true (that conditional is a page/form-level concern, not a reason to keep the pattern a raw String).
   - `receiptId: Option[UUID]` stays a pass-through context member (not a field).

## Acceptance criteria

- `web` compiles.
- No `FormData` under `net/wiringbits/forms` holds a raw user-input member any longer: every input is a `FormField` over a validated primitive and is in `fields`; the only non-`FormField` members are `Boolean`s and genuine non-edited context ids (`rowId`, `receiptId`).
- The new principle is documented as a section in `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` (flag/Not style) with the frontmatter description extended.
- New primitives `ExpNotes`, `ExpLocalTime`, and the id-selection field each have a spec; every changed `FormData` has an updated/added `*FormDataSpec`; all pass. Describe blocks are method-only.
- No `.trusted` on user-entered/derived values in any touched file; validated fields seeded with raw values; submit gated on `isValid` (no hand-written required checks).
- No changes outside `web/`; no API request/response model changes; nothing added to `lib/`.
- All reviewer gates in `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` satisfied.
- Repo is public: no PII in code, commits, or the PR description.

Commit per form/primitive so partial progress is reviewable. Open a PR when done.

resultJson.description:
Make every user-entered input on a web `FormData` a `FormField` over a validated primitive, then fix the five forms that still break that rule. Today `ExpenseFormData`, `ReceiptConfirmFormData`, `BulkExpenseFormData`, `BankRowRefundFormData` and `BankRowExpenseFormData` still keep notes, time, merchant ids, rule patterns and split rows as raw `String`/tuple members. Those members skip live validation and are left out of `isValid`. The pages then parse them by hand at submit, using `Try(UUID.fromString)` / `Try(LocalTime.parse)` / `Try(BigDecimal(_))` and dropping anything that fails without telling the user. After this epic, the only non-`FormField` members allowed on a `FormData` are `Boolean`s and non-edited context ids (`rowId`, `receiptId`). Every other member is a `FormField` in `fields`. It is seeded with the raw source value, and submit is gated on `isValid`.

The work happens in four steps. First, the rule is written up as a reviewer section in `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`. Second, three web-only primitives are added, each with its input objects and a spec: `ExpNotes` (bounded text, max 500), `ExpLocalTime` (ISO HH:mm[:ss]) and `ExpOptionalId` (blank = None, otherwise a well-formed UUID), plus a small validated `mui` select widget for choosing an existing entity by id. Third, the five FormData classes and the pages that render them are migrated. Split rows become a shared case class of FormFields, ids come from the validated select, and the receipt merchant becomes an `ExistingOrNewValue` pick-or-create resolved through `MerchantResolver`. Fourth, each changed FormData gets an updated spec.

Scope: only `web/` and `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` change. No API request/response models change, nothing is added to `lib/`, and new types live under `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits`. One cross-field rule stays at page level: "splits must cover the amount" (`ExpenseFormSplits.splitsError`). Commit once per primitive/form. The repo is public, so keep PII out of code and commits.

tasks.title: Document the 'every FormData input is a validated FormField' rule in the frontend reviewer
tasks.description:
Edit `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md` only. Add a new section, e.g. `## Every FormData input is a validated FormField`, right after `## Seed validated fields with the raw value`, next to the other FormData sections. Use the same 'Flag … / Not: …' prose style as the existing sections.

What to flag: a `FormData` subclass under `net/wiringbits/forms` that holds a raw `String`, `BigDecimal`, `Int`, `UUID`, `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, or a tuple/list of these as a user input. Also flag a `FormField` input that is missing from `fields` (so `isValid` doesn't cover it). The section states what each kind of input should be:
- text: a `WrappedString`-style primitive with a max length
- number: a bounded positive primitive like `PositiveBigDecimal`
- date/time: a parsed primitive like `ExpLocalDate` / `ExpLocalTime`
- picked id: a field whose validator enforces the id format (blank or a well-formed id)
- pick-or-create: `ExistingOrNewValue` resolved through the shared resolver
- a list of rows (e.g. splits): a row case class of FormFields whose fields are flattened into `fields`

Not: a `Boolean` checkbox/toggle; a pass-through context id the form carries but the user never edits (`rowId`, `receiptId`), which is a constructor input and not bound to an editable control; a field that only matters while an opt-in `Boolean` on the same FormData is on, which may be added to `fields` only while that opt-in is on.

Also extend the frontmatter `description:` line with a short clause such as `; every FormData input a FormField over a validated primitive (only Booleans and non-edited context ids stay raw)`. Write review instructions only, with no roadmap or future notes. Verify by reading the file back. No build is needed.

tasks.title: Add ExpNotes bounded-text primitive with inputs and spec
tasks.description:
Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpNotes.scala`, cloned from `lib/common/.../CategoryDescription.scala`:
- `class ExpNotes private (val string: String) extends WrappedString`
- `object ExpNotes extends WrappedString.Companion[ExpNotes]` with `val MaxLength: Int = 500`
- `validate`: the trimmed length must be <= MaxLength, or return Invalid with `s"Notes must be $MaxLength characters or less"`. A Valid result keeps the trimmed value and the original input.
- `trusted`
- `def parse(string): Either[String, ExpNotes]`, same shape as `ExpLocalDate.parse`
- `given optionalValidator: TextValidator[Option[ExpNotes]]`: a blank input gives `Valid(input, None)`, anything else wraps `validate`, as `ExpLocalDate`/`PositiveBigDecimal` do.

`WrappedString.Companion` should already provide the `given TextValidator[ExpNotes]`; check how `ExpRulePattern`/`RulePatternInput` compile. If it doesn't, add `given validator` explicitly.

In `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/inputs/expInputs.scala`, add `object NotesInput extends ValidatedTextInput[ExpNotes]` and `object OptionalNotesInput extends ValidatedTextInput[Option[ExpNotes]]`, and update the imports.

Add the spec `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpNotesSpec.scala` (plain ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec`, `Matchers.*`, no jsdom). Describe blocks are method-only: `"validate"`, `"parse"`, `"optionalValidator"`. Cover:
- a valid value round-trips through `.string`
- exactly 500 characters is accepted and 501 is rejected with the message
- `parse` returns Right/Left
- the optional validator maps blank/whitespace to `Some(None)`, wraps a valid value, and rejects an over-limit one

Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpNotesSpec"`.

tasks.title: Add ExpLocalTime parsed time primitive with inputs and spec
tasks.description:
Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpLocalTime.scala`, mirroring `ExpLocalDate.scala` line for line:
- `class ExpLocalTime private (val value: java.time.LocalTime)` with `toString = value.toString`
- `validate` uses `Try(LocalTime.parse(string.trim))`. ISO parsing accepts both `HH:mm` and `HH:mm:ss`. On failure return Invalid with the error `"Time must be in HH:MM format"`.
- `trusted(value: LocalTime)`, `given validator: TextValidator[ExpLocalTime]`, `parse: Either[String, ExpLocalTime]`, and `given optionalValidator: TextValidator[Option[ExpLocalTime]]` (blank gives None)

In `expInputs.scala`, add `object TimeInput extends ValidatedTextInput[ExpLocalTime]` and `object OptionalTimeInput extends ValidatedTextInput[Option[ExpLocalTime]]`.

Add the spec `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpLocalTimeSpec.scala` with method-only describe blocks (`"validate"`, `"parse"`, `"optionalValidator"`). Cover:
- `"09:15"` round-trips to `"09:15"`; `"09:15:30"` is accepted; surrounding whitespace is trimmed
- `"25:00"`, `"9.15"`, `"abc"` and blank are rejected with the message
- `parse` returns Right/Left
- the optional validator maps blank to `Some(None)`, wraps a valid time, and rejects a malformed one

Do not copy the type-qualified describe names from `ExpLocalDateSpec`. Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpLocalTimeSpec"`.

tasks.title: Add ExpOptionalId validator, a validated select widget, and the id-select input
tasks.description:
1. Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpOptionalId.scala` with `object ExpOptionalId`:
- `def validate(string: String): ValidationResult[Option[UUID]]`: blank/whitespace gives `Valid(string, None)`; otherwise `Try(UUID.fromString(string.trim))`, giving `Valid(string, Some(id))` or `Invalid(input = string, error = "Select a valid entry")`
- `def parse(string): Either[String, Option[UUID]]`
- `given validator: TextValidator[Option[UUID]] = validate(_)`

UUID's companion is a Java class and is not in implicit scope, so callers must pass `(using ExpOptionalId.validator)` or import it explicitly.

2. Create `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/core/widgets/ValidatedSelectInput.scala`. It is the select analogue of `ValidatedTextInput`: `abstract class ValidatedSelectInput[T: TextValidator]` with plain-Scala `Props(field: FormField[T], options: Seq[(String, String)] /* value -> label */, onChange: ValidationResult[T] => Unit, disabled: Boolean = false, noneLabel: Option[String] = Some("(none)"))`. Render `mui.TextField.outlined().select(true)` with `id`/`name` derived from `props.field.name`, plus `label`, `required`, `error`, `helperText` and `value = field input`. Children are `mui.MenuItem`s, an optional blank `""` item first, then each option keyed by its value. `onChange` runs the validator on the selected value. All `dom`/`asInstanceOf` interop stays inside the component, and no literal `withKey` is used.

3. In `expInputs.scala`, add `object OptionalIdSelectInput extends ValidatedSelectInput[Option[UUID]](using ExpOptionalId.validator)`.

4. Add the spec `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms/ExpOptionalIdSpec.scala` with method-only describe blocks (`"validate"`, `"parse"`). Cover: blank/whitespace gives `Some(None)`; a well-formed UUID gives `Some(Some(id))` and keeps the input; `"not-a-uuid"` is rejected with the message; `parse` returns Right/Left.

Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpOptionalIdSpec"`, then `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Migrate BulkExpenseFormData notes to a validated ExpNotes field
tasks.description:
`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BulkExpenseFormData.scala`:
- Change `notes: String` to `notes: FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]` and add it to `fields`.
- `initial` seeds it as `new FormField(label = "Notes (optional)", name = "notes", required = false, value = Some(ExpNotes.optionalValidator("")))`.
- `submitRequest` gets `n <- notes.valueOpt` and passes `notes = n.map(_.string)`. `Resolved.notes` stays `Option[String]`, so the page's API call is unchanged.

`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/expenses/BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala` (around lines 470-478): replace the raw `mui.TextField` bound to `formData.notes` with `OptionalNotesInput.component(OptionalNotesInput.Props(field = formData.notes, disabled = <existing disabled flag>, onChange = v => setFormData(cur => cur.copy(notes = cur.notes.updated(v)))))`. Keep the submit button gated on `isValid` as it already is.

Update `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BulkExpenseFormDataSpec.scala`:

- a value resolves (trimmed) to `Some`

Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *BulkExpenseFormDataSpec"` and `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Migrate BankRowExpenseFormData notes and rule pattern to validated fields
tasks.description:
`web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/BankRowExpenseFormData.scala`:

- `rulePattern: String` becomes `rulePattern: FormField[ExpRulePattern]` (`label = "Rule pattern"`, `name = "rulePattern"`, `required = true`), seeded raw with `Some(ExpRulePattern.validate(row.description))`.

tasks.title: Migrate ExpenseFormData (time, merchant id, notes, split rows) and ExpensesPage
tasks.description:
1. New shared row type `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/forms/ExpenseSplitRow.scala`:
- `case class ExpenseSplitRow(key: Int, category: FormField[Option[UUID]], amount: FormField[PositiveBigDecimal])`. `key` is a non-edited row identity used for unique field names and the React key.
- Companion helpers: `def blank(prefix: String, key: Int)`, `def seeded(prefix, key, categoryId: String, amount: String)` (seeds via `ExpOptionalId.validate` / `PositiveBigDecimal.validate` with raw strings), `def nextKey(rows: List[ExpenseSplitRow]): Int = rows.map(_.key).maxOption.fold(0)(_ + 1)`.
- Field names are `s"$prefix-split-$key-category"` and `s"$prefix-split-$key-amount"`. Category is `required = false`; amount is `required = true`.

2. `ExpenseFormData`:
- `time: FormField[Option[ExpLocalTime]]`, `merchantId: FormField[Option[UUID]]` (label "Merchant (optional)"), `notes: FormField[Option[ExpNotes]]`, `splits: List[ExpenseSplitRow]`
- `fields = List(amount, date, time, merchantId, notes) ++ splits.flatMap(r => List(r.category, r.amount))`
- Add pure transitions `addSplit`, `removeSplit(key)`, `updateSplit(key, f)`.
- `Resolved`: `time: Option[LocalTime]`, `merchantId: Option[UUID]`, `notes: Option[String]`, `splits: List[(Option[UUID], BigDecimal)]`. Resolve every field via `valueOpt`; use `traverse`-style folding for the rows so any invalid row gives None.
- `initial`/`fromExpense` seed raw values: `e.time.fold("")(_.toString)`, `e.merchantId.fold("")(_.toString)`, `e.notes.getOrElse("")`, and the splits by `categoryId.toString`/`amount.toString`. Field names keep the `expense-create`/`expense-edit` prefixes.

3. `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/ExpenseFormSplits.scala`: add typed variants `createSplits(amount: BigDecimal, splits: List[(Option[UUID], BigDecimal)], merchants, merchantId: Option[UUID])` and `merchantDefaultSplits(merchants, merchantId: Option[UUID], amount)`. Rows with no category are dropped, matching today's `parseSplits`. Keep the String-based `parseSplits`/`createSplits` for now, because ReceiptsPage still uses them; the receipts task removes them. Extend `ExpenseFormSplitsSpec` for the typed variants.

4. `ExpensesPage.scala`:
- Delete `parseTime`/`parseMerchantId`.
- `toUpdateSplits`/`updateSplits` take the typed `List[(Option[UUID], BigDecimal)]` (update `ExpensesPageSpec`).
- `splitRemainder` sums `row.amount.valueOpt`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- `web/` (Scala.js + Slinky + MUI via ScalablyTyped `com.olvind.mui.muiMaterial.components as mui`) is the only code module touched. The sbt project id is `web`. Targeted runs: `sbt "web/testOnly *XSpec"`; typecheck with `CI=true sbt web/Test/compile`. Don't run the full `sbt test`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default node v16 fails at yarn install).
- `lib/common`, `lib/api`: READ ONLY. `ImportRuleMatcher` (lib/api/shared/.../api/utils) has MinPatternLength=3, MaxPatternLength=255 and `normalize`. `CategoryDescription` (lib/common/.../common/models) is the shape to clone for ExpNotes. API models such as `CreateExpense.Request(amount, date, time: Option[LocalTime], merchantId: Option[UUID], notes: Option[String], splits: List[CreateExpense.Split(categoryId: UUID, amount)])`, `UpdateExpense.Request` (same order), and `ConfirmReceipt.Request(amount: Option, date: Option, time, merchantId, notes, splits, parsedMerchantName: Option[String], rowId)` must NOT change. The server uses `parsedMerchantName` + `merchantId` only to auto-create a set_merchant rule.
- `.orca/reviewers/frontend.md`: reviewer rules (frontmatter `description` + "## Title / Flag… / Not:" sections). Existing gates that matter here: FormData carries a spec; required fields modeled on the field and submit gated on `isValid` via `useSubmit`'s `buttonDisabled(formData.isValid)`; seed validated fields with the raw value (no `.trim`/`.take`); js interop stays inside components with plain-Scala Props; no literal `.withKey("…")` in reusable components; pick-or-create goes through `CategoryResolver`/`MerchantResolver`; SafeHooks for dep lists; functional updater for setters derived from previous state.

FORM STACK (library `net.wiringbits.webapp.utils.slinkyUtils.forms.{FormData, FormField}`, validators `net.wiringbits.webapp.common.validators.{TextValidator, ValidationResult}`)
- `new FormField[T](label, name, required, value: Option[ValidationResult[T]] = None)`; `.updated(ValidationResult[T])`, `.valueOpt: Option[T]`, `.inputValue: String`, `.value`, `.name`, `.label`, `.required`.
- `FormData[R]`: override `fields: List[FormField[?]]` and `submitRequest: Option[R]`; it provides `isValid` and `formValidationErrors`.
- `ValidationResult.Valid(input, value)` / `.Invalid(input = …, error = …)`; `.toOption`, `.hasError`, `.errorMessage`, `.input`.
- `TextValidator[T]` is a SAM `String => ValidationResult[T]`.
- An optional field is seeded with `Some(X.optionalValidator(raw))` or `Some(ValidationResult.Valid("", None))`. An untouched (value=None) field yields `valueOpt` None, which breaks for-comprehensions, so always seed optional fields.
- Required untouched fields: value None leaves the form invalid with no error shown (see `BankRowRuleFormData.empty`).

PRIMITIVE TEMPLATES (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/forms)
- `ExpLocalDate.scala`: private-ctor class; companion with `validate`, `trusted`, `given validator: TextValidator[T]`, `parse: Either[String,T]`, `given optionalValidator: TextValidator[Option[T]]` (blank gives Valid(input, None)). Copy this shape for ExpLocalTime.
- `PositiveBigDecimal.scala` (`PositiveBigDecimalCompanion`, `.value: BigDecimal`, error messages like "Amount must be greater than zero").
- `ExpRuleFields.scala`: `ExpRulePattern extends WrappedString` (`.string`) via `WrappedString.Companion` (`net.wiringbits.webapp.common.models.WrappedString`), plus `ExpRuleDescription` (with optionalValidator) and `ExpRuleAmount`.
- `ExistingOrNewValue[T, Id](value: T, id: Option[Id])`.
- `ExistingSelections.merchant(m)/newMerchant(text)/category(c)/existingCategory(name,id)/defaultCategory(...)` return ValidationResult seeds; names are always validated.
- `SubmitHooks.useSubmit()` returns a Control with `isSubmitting`, `inputDisabled`, `error`, `begin/succeed/fail/reset`, `buttonDisabled(isValid)`.
- Each FormData has its own private `asOptional[T](ValidationResult[T]): ValidationResult[Option[T]]` helper, copied per file (BankRowRefund/BankRowExpense/BankRowRule).

INPUTS
- `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/core/widgets/ValidatedTextInput.scala`: `abstract class ValidatedTextInput[T: TextValidator]`, `Props(field, disabled=false, onChange: ValidationResult[T] => Unit, margin="dense", autoFocus=false)`. The label comes from `field.label`, the DOM id from `field.name`, and helperText is the error message.
- `ExpValidatedAutocompleteInput[Opt: ClassTag, T: TextValidator, Id, V](optionLabel, optionId)(using SelectionShape)`: `Props(field, options: Seq[Opt], label, onChange, disabled=false, fullWidth=true)`. The key is `field.name`.
- `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/ui/components/inputs/expInputs.scala` holds the instances: `AmountInput` (PositiveBigDecimal), `PositiveBigDecimalInput` (Option), `DateInput`, `RulePatternInput`, `RuleAmountInput`, `RuleDescriptionInput`, `MerchantAutocompleteInput`, `CategoryAutocompleteInput`, `OptionalCategoryAutocompleteInput`, `OptionalMerchantAutocompleteInput` (options `GetMerchants.Response.Merchant`). New input objects go here.
- Implicit-scope gotcha: `ValidatedTextInput[Option[ExpNotes]]` finds the given in the `ExpNotes` companion (Scala 3 searches the companions of type args). `Option[UUID]` does NOT (UUID is a Java class), so pass `(using ExpOptionalId.validator)` explicitly.
- Today's mui select pattern (ExpensesPage `merchantOptions`): `mui.TextField.outlined().select(true).label(..).value(str).onChange(e => e.target.asInstanceOf[dom.HTMLInputElement].value)(mui.MenuItem.normal()(label).value(v).withKey(v).build*)`.

RESOLVERS (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages)
- `MerchantResolver.findOrCreateMerchantOpt(client, merchants, selection: Option[ExistingOrNewValue[MerchantName, UUID]], categoryId: Option[UUID])(using ec): Future[Option[(UUID, Option[GetMerchants.Response.Merchant])]]`. It is `private[pages]`, so subpackages such as `pages.receipts` can use it.
- `CategoryResolver.findOrCreateCategory(client, categories, selection)`.
- Usage example plus the retry-safe `withResolvedMerchant` pattern: `bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala` ~lines 235-255 and `BankRowExpenseFormData.withResolvedMerchant`.
- `ExpenseFormSplits` (pages/ExpenseFormSplits.scala): `splitsError(amount, List[BigDecimal]): Option[String]` holds the page-level cross-field rule. `parseSplits`/`createSplits`/`merchantDefaultSplits` are String-based today and are shared by ExpensesPage and ReceiptsPage.

FILES TO CHANGE (current raw members)
- forms/ExpenseFormData.scala: `time`, `merchantId`, `notes: String`, `splits: List[(String,String)]`. `initial` and `fromExpense(e: GetExpenses.Response.Expense)` use field-name prefixes `expense-create`/`expense-edit`, because the create and edit forms can be on screen together.
- pages/expenses/ExpensesPage.scala (object `ExpenseList`, ~1245 lines): `parseTime`/`parseMerchantId` (~326), `save`, `handleCreate`/`handleUpdate`, `toUpdateSplits`/`updateSplits` (~256, tested in ExpensesPageSpec ~379), `splitRemainder`, `formFields` (~451), `merchantOptions`, `splitRow`, `splitsSection` (index React keys).
- forms/ReceiptConfirmFormData.scala: `time`, `merchantId`, `merchantInput`, `notes`, `splits: List[(catId, catInput, amt)]`, `parsedMerchantName`, `rowId`. `fromReceipt(r, merchants, categories, rules)` uses `ReceiptsLogic.resolveMerchant` (returns `Option[{merchantId, categoryId, description}]`).
- pages/receipts/ReceiptsPage.scala: `handleConfirm` ~349, `confirm` ~361 (parses time/merchantId by hand), `merchantAutocomplete` ~573 (raw MuiCompat + a "reset" reason string), `splitRow`/`splitsSection` ~599-680, confirm form render ~930-985. Batch confirm (~500) builds `ConfirmReceipt.Request` independently; leave it alone. `ReceiptsLogic.ReceiptMode.Confirming(receiptId, form)` / `withForm`.
- forms/BulkExpenseFormData.scala + pages/expenses/BulkExpenseCreationPage.scala (~473 notes TextField).
- forms/BankRowRefundFormData.scala + pages/bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateRefundForm.scala (~153; notes seed from `BankRowCreateExpenseForm.initialNotes`).
- forms/BankRowExpenseFormData.scala + pages/bankstatementreview/BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala: notes ~380; rulePattern is used in TWO places, the NeedsAlias merchant-alias input (~424, "Leave blank for no rule") and the category-rule opt-in input (~444). `aliasToCreate`/`categoryRuleToCreate` (~132-152) are tested in BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec.

DESIGN DECISIONS (made in planning; follow them)
- Split rows use a shared `ExpenseSplitRow(key: Int, category: FormField[Option[UUID]], amount: FormField[PositiveBigDecimal])` in `net.wiringbits.forms`. `key` comes from max+1 and is used for unique field names and the React key (not the list index). Rows with no category are dropped at resolve, matching today's `parseSplits`; the coverage rule then catches the mismatch.
- The receipt split category becomes a select of existing categories (`OptionalIdSelectInput`). It never created categories before.
- The receipt merchant becomes an `ExistingOrNewValue` pick-or-create via `OptionalMerchantAutocompleteInput` + `MerchantResolver`. `parsedMerchantName` leaves the form; the page reads it from the receipt (`r.merchantName`) at confirm. A rule pointing at a merchant id missing from the list now seeds a blank merchant.
- BankRowExpense `rulePattern` is a required `FormField[ExpRulePattern]` that is in `fields` only while `categoryRuleOptIn` is true. That is the form-level conditional: a row description <3 or >255 chars must not block an expense when no rule is wanted. `Resolved.rulePattern: Option[String]` comes from `valueOpt`; the alias path treats None as "no alias".
- `ExpNotes.validate` stores the trimmed string (value-level normalization like CategoryDescription). Seeds still pass the raw text.

CONVENTIONS
- Specs: plain ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec` + `org.scalatest.matchers.must.Matchers.*`, no jsdom, under `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/{forms,ui/forms}`. Describe blocks name the method only (`"validate"`, `"submitRequest"`, `"fromExpense"`). Don't copy `ExpLocalDateSpec`'s type-qualified names. Reference spec shapes: `ExpLocalDateSpec`, `BankRowRuleFormDataSpec`, `ExpenseFormDataSpec`, `ReceiptConfirmFormDataSpec`.
- Never `.trusted` a user/derived value. Never `.trim`/`.take` a seed. No hand-written required checks in `formValidationErrors`. No `setTimeout`/hacks. No silent defaults (if a parse fails, the field shows invalid).
- Scaladoc each new type briefly, in the style of the existing files. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before committing. Commit per primitive/form. No PII anywhere (public repo).
